name: Redington Ltd
title: Redington Ltd - 532805 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Redington Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to INR34,966 crores and PAT 77% to INR486 crores, helped by PC price-led stock-and-sell.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR34,966 crores (+34% YoY), EBITDA INR751 crores (+67%) and PAT INR486 crores (+77%), with profit growth outpacing revenue. Excluding Arena, revenue grew 41% to INR33,794 crores and profit was INR517 crores, which management called the best ever. India grew 63% on top line and was the strongest geography, while Middle East & Africa grew 15% despite the West Asia crisis, with UAE and Saudi softening. Management attributed a large part of ESG growth to component-shortage-driven price increases and channel stocking, and flagged that large data-center deals will dilute margin percentage. Arena continued to lose money (INR64 crores total, INR31 crores Redington share).

financial_highlights.value: INR64 crores total; INR31 crores Redington share

financial_highlights.change: vs INR31 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Top line grew 63% and PAT 60%; Mobility, Endpoint, Technology and Software Solutions all grew strong double digits. Professional services grew triple digits.

segments.name: Middle East & Africa
segments.commentary: Region grew 15% YoY; GCC and Levant grew 95% and Africa 39%, while UAE declined about 3% and Saudi declined about 7%.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Grew 21% YoY, 35% of top line; growth tied to premium segment and direct retail in India, but supply constrained demand.

segments.name: Endpoint Solutions (ESG)
segments.commentary: Grew 35% YoY, 29% of top line; growth led by component-shortage price increases, with unit growth flat to single digit. AI PCs were 36% of India commercial revenue.

segments.name: Technology Solutions (TSG)
segments.commentary: Grew 50% YoY, 17% of top line; about INR1,000 crores of large deals in the quarter, roughly INR700 crores from India data-center business.

segments.name: Software Solutions (SSG)
segments.commentary: Grew 52% YoY (about 53% cited), 17% of top line vs 15% a year ago; cloud grew 67%, SISA 55%, Rest of World 80%. Services almost doubled and were about 2.5% of revenue.

segments.name: Arena (Turkey)
segments.commentary: Loss of INR64 crores; debt down to $90 million from $120-130 million; interest including factoring INR37 crores vs INR69 crores a year ago. Management expects losses to continue this year.

guidance_outlook: Q2 expected to be a strong quarter, driven by mobility NPI launches, though this depends on the NPI SKU range.
Q3 expected to see good pickup into the festive season; management declined to forecast beyond that.
Management sees at least 2-3 months of channel inventory and expects component shortages to persist for multiple quarters.
Data-center funnel is multiple times the INR1,000 crore Q1 large-deal revenue for the next few quarters; AI hardware not expected to taper for 4-6 quarters.
Large deals will dilute gross and EBITDA margin percentage, but ROCE will not be compromised; large deal profitability will not match normal profitability.
Finance cost run-rate: management said Q1 levels can be taken as steady-state quarterly numbers.
Arena: management expects losses to continue in the current year and is evaluating structural options.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity-expansion figures were discussed on the call.
Mobility growth was constrained by product supply and capacity, per management.
Data-center deal backlog is described as multiple times the quarter's large-deal revenue.
demand_pricing: PC prices have risen an estimated 25-50% over the last 2-3 quarters (some SKUs about 50%); PC unit volume grew flat to single digit.
Channel is stocking up; management estimates about 2-3 months of inventory in the channel, and says inventory build spans distributors and Tier 2 partners.
Apple raised prices last; most PC OEMs and Android vendors have also raised prices. Management says little room for further price rises remains.
UAE and Saudi: government and corporate projects being postponed; supply delays of about 30 days; freight and warehousing costs up, about $3 million extra in the quarter.
Arena: hypercompetitive Turkey market with gross margin compression; revenue roughly halved.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 performance was driven by pre-buying ahead of chip price hikes, and what is channel inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stock-and-sell effect is largely in ESG PCs; channel holds about 2-3 months of inventory, and the build is across distributors and Tier 2 partners.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on large deals and India mobility growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR700 crores of the INR1,000 crore large deals came from India data centers; funnel is multiple times that. Premium smartphone share gains helped Mobility, but management is unsure if demand holds after price rises.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East demand in UAE and Saudi, and cost pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: UAE was down about 3-4% and Saudi slightly more; some freight and warehousing cost passed on, while about $3 million of extra cost sat in opex.

qa_highlights.question: Why Arena losses persist and what is the end goal?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue halved, margins compressed and opex inflated by 35-40%; management says structural options are being evaluated and losses may continue this year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the working capital reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days rose industry-wide, but better payable days, especially in Middle East from additional vendor credit, offset it; spikes occurred within the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance costs rise 74% QoQ, and what was the INR147 crore tax refund?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher revenue and inventory days raised interest, and market rates firmed though central bank rates were unchanged. The refund related to contested past-year demands that the company won.

risks_watch: Channel inventory build and PC price-led demand: management expects consumer demand to weaken as prices rise; watch unit volumes versus value.
Middle East: UAE and Saudi softening, delayed government and corporate projects, about 30-day supply delays, and receivable provisioning (cautious provisioning in Saudi).
Arena: continued losses, debt reduction, and possible structural change.
Finance cost rising with inventory days and firming market interest rates.
Margin dilution from large data-center deals; Q2 and Q3 seasonality is uncertain given higher ASPs.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India, TSG and SSG growth and on working capital, but cautious on consumer PC/smartphone demand, Middle East softening and Arena, where management repeatedly said the problem is not easy to solve.
